message: Bound FalkorDB to recent live state and require fresh multi-probe, multi-AS evidence so stale or broadly failing probes cannot dominate production incident detection
Added transit relationship drill-down with current endpoint-AS RIPE test evidence and ClickHouse loss/RTT history while explicitly avoiding causal claims about the selected hop
Guard empty FalkorDB aggregates and buffer JSON responses so non-finite values cannot produce HTTP 200 responses with empty bodies.
Define target incidents as packet-weighted, cross-network loss regressions from a healthy 24-hour baseline; exclude broadly failing probes and persistent ICMP non-responders.

Cache public RIPE Atlas probe inventory as FalkorDB node properties in a paced background worker; keep checked and successfully updated timestamps separate so unavailable IDs do not look enriched or trigger repeated requests.
Registered the existing IP detail API in the React router and added the missing IP topology page so every generated /ip link resolves to observed hop evidence.

Route correlation uses route-level ClickHouse history for commonality, per-hop baselines and multi-probe agreement for signal quality, and FalkorDB only for bounded live enrichment; correlated ICMP RTT is presented as investigation evidence rather than fault proof.

Use a single production Ripestream container for ingestion, the embedded UI/API, alerts, and graph maintenance; publish it on host port 3000 while keeping ClickHouse and FalkorDB private and persistent.

Download GeoLite2-ASN atomically from a configured HTTPS object URL at Ripestream container startup, with optional Cloudflare Access headers and SHA-256 verification, so the licensed MMDB and storage credentials stay outside Git and the image.

Use only Cloudflare R2's authenticated S3 API for the production GeoLite2-ASN runtime download, using bucket-scoped read credentials and jurisdiction-specific endpoints; do not pass the parent API token or expose the bucket publicly.

Do not bind Ripestream's dashboard to host port 3000 in Dokploy; listen and expose only container port 3000, with inbound access handled by Dokploy's domain proxy to avoid cross-application port collisions.

Match Ripestream's internal HTTP listener to Dokploy's persistent Traefik target port 8080 while retaining expose-only networking, so no host port is allocated and other services can continue using host port 3000.

Replace production PING JSON parsing with typed ClickHouse columns to prevent allocation failures; bound route commonality memory with approximate distinct aggregation, limited threads, and smaller blocks; return 503 for backend query failures.

Make schema splitting SQL-comment and quote aware after a semicolon in a migration comment caused ClickHouse Empty query on startup; give production ClickHouse an env-configurable 8 GiB container limit while retaining bounded queries.

Bound route-correlation history by prefiltering exact recent candidates, deterministically sampling one quarter of the 24-hour baseline, and enabling ClickHouse external aggregation/sort spill instead of extending API deadlines.

Make docker-compose.yml the self-contained server deployment: build Ripestream, publish host port 8080 for Cloudflare Tunnel, persist app data, and keep ClickHouse/FalkorDB private to the Compose network.

Route correlation now reads ingest-time typed traceroute hop observations; a guarded 31-hour startup backfill preserves existing history, and the UI avoids automatic failure retries. Dense local benchmark: 0.387s versus the prior 20s deadline.

Use bounded offset pagination for graph worklists: fetch one sentinel row for has_more, execute cross-field filters server-side, and disable Probes polling to prevent live reordering during investigation.

Replaced generic Loader2 with an RJ45/Cat5e CableSpinner; paginated worklists use FetchingOverlay on isFetching&&isPlaceholderData so users see progress without blanking rows or flashing on 30s background refetch

Probe→Targets and Target→Probes now use separate paginated relationship endpoints over the same retained PING-edge semantics; detail summaries report anchored total counts instead of capped array lengths.
IP detail incoming and outgoing NEXT_HOP relationships now use anchored total counts plus independently filtered/paginated direction pages, replacing the silent 50-edge caps.
Compute IP route graphs with independent cycle-safe upstream/downstream NEXT_HOP traversals and explicit depth/node/edge truncation metadata so the UI never labels a safety-bounded graph complete.

Register the IP route-graph page shell eagerly while keeping react-force-graph lazy inside the page, preventing direct deep links from failing during frontend asset-set transitions; distinguish true 404s from runtime load errors.
Retain ClickHouse raw and typed-hop rows for 24 hours from ingestion via table TTLs, and align FalkorDB's default janitor horizon to 24 hours so both high-volume stores remain bounded.
Keep ClickHouse on a 24-hour rolling TTL but retain FalkorDB observations for only 6 hours because the graph is a smaller live-state projection; preserve the independent 30-minute health window.
Apply ClickHouse TTL changes with materialize_ttl_after_modify=0 so schema startup remains bounded on populated tables while normal background TTL merges enforce retention.
Measure RIPE Atlas ingestion at pipeline ingress and expose a fixed 60-second in-memory snapshot so the sidebar reflects stream reads without adding database query load.
Destination ASNIssues no longer double-scans PING edges for noisy-probe prefiltering; use MinSourceASes consensus and raise FalkorDB query/read timeouts so /asns does not 502 behind Cloudflare Tunnel
